papers_read.title_as_printed: Machine Learning-Based Prediction Models for Cognitive Decline Progression: A Comparative Study in Multilingual Settings Using Speech Analysis (Ceyhan, Bek, Onal-Suzek, 2024)
Cross-lingual detection of mild cognitive impairment based on temporal parameters of spontaneous speech (Gosztolya et al., Computer Speech & Language 2021)

what_each_reports.P-158: ADReSS AD vs non-AD, acoustic features, random forest: 95% accuracy in 10-fold CV over speed-augmented segments; 73% on the ADReSS held-out test set. MUDC (60 Turkish patients, all from a dementia outpatient clinic, described as MCI, stratified by MMSE): MLP 94%; cross-language 72% and 76%.
what_each_reports.P-58: MCI vs healthy controls (Petersen criteria), 15 ASR-derived temporal speech parameters, SVM with speaker-wise leave-one-out nested CV, metrics at equal error rate: English (n=33: 14 MCI/19 HC) accuracy 84.8%, AUC 0.932; Hungarian (n=33: 13 MCI/20 HC) accuracy 75.8%, AUC 0.727 (filler-only 90.9%, AUC 0.912); cross-lingual 78.8%/75.8%; overall range 67-92%.

quantity_a: Accuracy for Alzheimer's dementia vs non-AD from acoustic features of Cookie Theft descriptions (ADReSS), segment-augmented 10-fold CV.
quantity_b: Speaker-level accuracy (at EER threshold) for MCI vs healthy controls from temporal/hesitation parameters of 'describe your previous day' monologues recorded over the phone (English New York and Hungarian Szeged samples).
incompatible_if_same: No: P-58's reported range (67-92%) reaches 92% on a 33-speaker sample, and P-158's held-out ADReSS test accuracy (73%) sits inside that range; nothing here excludes the other.

gates.task: mismatch: AD vs non-AD (P-158's 95%) vs MCI vs HC (P-58). P-158's MUDC 94% is also not MCI vs HC: all MUDC participants are clinic patients described as MCI, stratified by MMSE bands.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: ADReSS/Pitt (and MUDC) vs the New York/Szeged MCI-HC recordings.
gates.validation_tier: nominally internal for both; P-158 CV over augmented segments of the same recordings, P-58 speaker-wise nested leave-one-out.
gates.modality_family: speech family for both; input representation differs (spectral/MFCC acoustic features vs ASR-derived articulation-rate and pause parameters).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: accuracy on different diagnostic contrasts; P-58 reports EER-thresholded accuracy and a range, not a single estimate.
performance_validity: flag not tripped (95% < 0.97); P-158's 95% is a weak estimate (segment-level augmented CV, 73% on held-out test).
grounds: P-158's 95% accuracy is for Alzheimer's dementia vs non-AD speakers on ADReSS, while P-58's 67-92% is for MCI vs healthy controls, so the population behind the label differs.

The datasets, speech tasks (picture description vs phone monologue) and features (spectral acoustic vs temporal/pause parameters) differ, so the dataset gate fails and the input representation differs, with no waiver on record.
Even setting the estimand aside, the values overlap: P-58's range reaches 92%, and P-158's own held-out test accuracy is 73%.

evidence_quotes.quote: it is a balanced dataset composed of cognitively normal (CN) patients and those suffering from Alzheimer's disease (AD)
we repeated the same Cookie Theft picture exam in Turkish on 60 patients with mild cognitive impairment in the MUDC.
We achieved 73% accuracy for the labels (dementia or not)

the language on which the ASR system was trained only slightly affects the MCI classification performance, because we got quite similar scores (67-92%) as we did in the monolingual cases (67-92% as well).
we did not create separate training and test sets, but opted for speaker-wise cross-validation (CV)

record_defects: dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong: ADReSS/MUDC (P-158) vs the New York/Szeged recordings (P-58).
modality_family 'speech_language' is correct, but both claims are labelled 'T1' although P-158's 95% is AD vs non-AD.
claim_b '67-92% range' is a span of accuracy, precision, recall and specificity across feature subsets, not one estimate; gap_magnitude 0.28 is computed from its lower end.
claim_a still cites P-276 (repointed to P-158).
what_would_change_the_verdict: A P-158 subject-level MCI-vs-healthy-control result would be needed; even then the values would have to fall outside P-58's reported range.
